idea: Research quality scoring service for allocators
buyer: Allocators assessing whether a manager's research is any good
pain: Allocators cannot judge research quality, only returns
v1: A scored assessment of one manager's research output
verdict: Genuinely novel and she is unusually qualified, but nobody has ever bought this and the category may not exist.

why.distribution: Reachable via her husband's network but as introductions, not direct relationships.
why.demand: Nobody buys this today and allocators have not asked for it - this is invention, not discovery.
why.fmf: She has read thousands of research notes and can judge quality better than almost any allocator.
why.revenue_structure: One-off assessments tied to allocation decisions.
why.defensibility: A scoring methodology plus accumulated comparative data would genuinely compound.
why.tailwind: Flat; allocators focus on returns and process, not written quality.
why.ceiling: £7.5k x 27 assessments = £200k, which assumes a buying habit that does not exist.

ceiling_arithmetic: £7.5k x 27 assessments = £200k, entirely contingent on creating a category from nothing. Realistic year one if it works at all: 3-5 = £22-37k.
carries: A real methodological edge and a defensible dataset if the category ever forms.
kills: Demand at 1. Allocators have not asked for this, and educating a market is the most expensive thing a solo founder can attempt.
test: Ask four allocators how they currently judge research quality.
test_pass: They admit they cannot and want a method.
test_fail: They say returns and process are the only things that matter.
